domain: team dinner at a Middle Eastern restaurant
base_instruction: You are a helpful restaurant recommendation and meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a group dinner by tracking who is attending, their dietary restrictions, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a team dinner at a Middle Eastern restaurant. You will introduce your group (me, Sarah, Dev, Marcus) with their dietary issues in one burst. Over several turns, Marcus will drop out, Sarah's celiac will be revealed as a misdiagnosis, and Dev's wife Priya will join late with her own constraints (pregnant + tree nut allergy). At the end you will present a list of menu items and ask if there are any issues. You never hint at what the problems might be.

ground_truth.answer: Current diners: me, Sarah, Dev, Priya. Active constraints: Dev (Jain — no meat, no eggs, no root vegetables including onions and garlic), Priya (tree nut allergy + pregnant). Sarah has NO restrictions (celiac was misdiagnosis). Marcus is not attending (sesame allergy irrelevant). Dish analysis: (1) Lamb shawarma platter — PROBLEM for Dev (meat, Jain diet forbids it). (2) Hummus with tahini — tahini is made from sesame, but Marcus (sesame allergy) is no longer coming, so this is FINE. However, hummus contains garlic — PROBLEM for Dev (Jain, no root vegetables/garlic). (3) Falafel wrap with garlic sauce — garlic sauce is a PROBLEM for Dev (Jain, no garlic/root vegetables). (4) Beef kibbeh — PROBLEM for Dev (meat). (5) Pistachio baklava — PROBLEM for Priya (tree nut allergy, pistachios specifically). (6) Fattoush salad — FINE for everyone (it's a vegetable salad with no root vegetable issues for standard fattoush).
required_elements: Lamb shawarma platter is problematic for Dev because it contains meat and Dev follows a Jain diet
Hummus with tahini is problematic for Dev because hummus typically contains garlic, which is a root vegetable forbidden in Jain diet
Falafel wrap with garlic sauce is problematic for Dev because garlic is a root vegetable forbidden in Jain diet
Beef kibbeh is problematic for Dev because it contains meat and Dev follows a Jain diet
Pistachio baklava is problematic for Priya because she has a tree nut allergy and pistachios are tree nuts
Fattoush salad is fine for everyone currently attending
forbidden_elements: Flagging hummus with tahini as problematic due to sesame (Marcus is no longer attending, his sesame allergy is irrelevant)
Flagging any dish as problematic for Sarah due to gluten (her celiac was a misdiagnosis, she has no restrictions)
Saying Dev cannot eat sesame or tahini (Jain diet does not restrict sesame)
Flagging fattoush salad as problematic for Dev (standard fattoush uses lettuce, tomatoes, cucumber, radish, and herbs — no onion or garlic required)
Over-generalizing Priya's tree nut allergy to all nuts including sesame or peanuts
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 turns at a Middle Eastern restaurant. The agent must track: (1) Dev is from a Jain family and still follows traditions → Jain vegetarian → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables including onions and garlic (multi-step inferential chain), (2) Marcus EXITS mid-conversation (his sesame allergy becomes irrelevant — this is the over-generalization trap since hummus with tahini contains sesame but Marcus isn't coming), (3) Sarah's celiac constraint is REMOVED (misdiagnosis corrected), (4) Priya JOINS LATE with two constraints: tree nut allergy (direct) and pregnancy (inferential — should avoid raw/undercooked meat). The probe includes 6 items: lamb shawarma (meat → Dev problem), hummus with tahini (contains garlic → Dev problem; contains sesame but Marcus gone → trap item that looks bad but isn't for sesame reasons), falafel wrap with garlic sauce (garlic → Dev problem), beef kibbeh (meat → Dev problem), pistachio baklava (tree nut → Priya problem), fattoush salad (fine for everyone). The key failure modes are: forgetting Priya (late-joiner), keeping Marcus's sesame constraint active (removed entity ghost), keeping Sarah's celiac active (removed constraint), and missing garlic as a root vegetable in Jain diet (inferential depth).

mechanism: Late-joiner with high-constraint: new person with strict needs arrives late
